title: Linked hubs
subtitle: Group this hub with others. A group has one primary hub, and the app is routed to it whichever hub it connects to. Both sides must confirm a link; discovered hubs never link on their own.
rarely_needed_body: You only need linked hubs when two places each have an always-on hub that can't reach the other, or when you already run several hubs and want to merge them. We recommend a single hub: install the node service on your other computers and add them under Computers.
tls_only_body: This hub has no TLS port yet, so it can't link to other hubs. Hubs always talk over TLS and check each other's public key fingerprint, even on a local network.
missing_title: This hub version doesn't support linking
missing_body: After you update the hub, you can see hubs found on your LAN, create and enter link codes, and check link status here.
linked_footer: Disconnecting revokes the link credentials on both sides and drops the link right away. To link again, exchange a new link code.
linked_empty: Not linked with any hub yet
linked_empty_body: On the other hub's admin page, choose Create link code. Then choose Add hub here: verify the other hub first, then paste the code.
discovered_footer: Hubs announcing themselves over mDNS on your LAN. Docker bridge networks don't receive these announcements; use Add hub and enter the address instead.
discovered_empty: No other hubs found on your LAN.
group_footer: The primary hub serves every app, keeps all state, and connects to every computer; member hubs hand their requests and computers to it. If the primary can't be reached it isn't replaced automatically; set a new one here when needed. Term {term}.
via_other_hub: Connected via another hub in the group
set_center_offline_hint: Can't reach this hub. Wait until it's online
now_center_self: This hub is now the primary
set_unreachable_self: Can't reach this hub. Try again when it's online.
set_unreachable_named: Can't reach "{name}". Try again when it's online.
set_center_body_self: Afterwards this hub manages the group's device credentials, push, sessions, and every computer. The app is routed to it whichever hub in the group it connects to.
set_center_body_named: Afterwards "{name}" manages the group's device credentials, push, sessions, and every computer. The app is routed to it whichever hub in the group it connects to.
set_center_body_demote_self: Afterwards this hub manages the group's device credentials, push, sessions, and every computer. The app is routed to it whichever hub in the group it connects to. The current primary, "{old}", becomes a member.
set_center_body_demote_named: Afterwards "{name}" manages the group's device credentials, push, sessions, and every computer. The app is routed to it whichever hub in the group it connects to. The current primary, "{old}", becomes a member.
old_center_offline: The current primary, "{old}", can't be reached. It becomes a member when it comes back.
code_hint_left: Paste it on the other hub's admin page under Linked hubs › Add hub, after verifying this hub. It works once and expires in {left}.
code_hint_expired: Paste it on the other hub's admin page under Linked hubs › Add hub, after verifying this hub. It works once. {expired}
code_expired: It has expired; close this and create a new one.
code_warning: A hub with this code can see all of this hub's computers. Only give it to your own hubs.
probe_ok: Check that the hub ID and public key fingerprint match what the other hub's Overview shows before you continue. If they don't match, don't link: you may have the wrong address, or someone in between is impersonating it.
probe_no_tls: The other hub has TLS off, so it can't link. Turn on TLS in its admin page under Network & access, restart that hub, then verify again.
code_field_hint: From the other hub's admin page under Linked hubs › Create link code. Valid for 10 minutes, works once
code_field_no_tls: The other hub needs TLS on before it can link
code_field_check_first: Verify the other hub's address first
